findings.claim: Current governance is fragmented: some rules address discrimination, monitoring data, protected activity, quotas, platform deactivation or emotion recognition, but no single recovered regime closes the full in-employment control loop.
The EU AI Act currently prohibits workplace emotion recognition while the broader high-risk employment duties remain pre-effective until 2 December 2027 under the current implementation timeline.
limits: System classification and exceptions require legal analysis.

findings.claim: Illinois now covers AI effects and notice across discipline, discharge and other employment conditions, but the cited text does not supply a complete explanation, appeal, health or survivor-bias protocol.

Clifford Number’s burden is therefore transaction-level: preserve data, construct, model, alert, context, support, human authority, decision, explanation, challenge and later learning before organizational silence is mistaken for validation.
limits: Normative estate synthesis; controls remain unadopted.

observations.claim: ICO guidance requires meaningful information, human intervention and challenge for covered solely automated decisions and requires active, competent human decision support rather than token involvement.
limits: Application is fact-specific and guidance under review.

observations.claim: The EU AI Act workplace emotion-recognition prohibition has applied since February 2025.
The current Commission timeline places Annex III employment and worker-management high-risk duties at 2 December 2027.
limits: Not operative on the wave date.

observations.claim: Illinois Public Act 103-0804 took effect on 1 January 2026 and reaches AI use affecting discipline, discharge and other employment conditions, including notice and protected-class discrimination limits.
The European Parliament adopted a nonbinding resolution requesting horizontal workplace algorithmic-management rules and stronger human-decision, information and participation controls.

The archived CFPB worker-surveillance release and Seattle deactivation litigation show additional score, report, notice and challenge pathways outside conventional HR law, but their temporal and jurisdictional limits remain material.
limits: Archived policy and preliminary-injunction ruling are not universal current law.

title: Temporal governance, human authority, and the complete adverse-AI receipt
